old.name: Es Baluard / Old Town around Santa Maria
old.text: The schist-paved upper warren climbing to the late-Gothic Església de Santa Maria (begun mid-16th c., on Carrer de Sant Isidre), whose Baroque gilt-wood altarpiece by Pau Costa frames the patroness, the Mare de Déu de l'Esperança. Streets average 3-4 m wide, paved in rastell — vertical slate slabs set on edge against the runoff.

old.text: The seafront ribbon below the old town, running along the bay past Plaça des Portitxó. Here stands Casa Serinyana, the modernist Casa Blava built 1913-15 — one of the few non-whitewashed facades in the village.

old.text: The dry torrent bed that splits the village and floods only in storms; its flat course hosts the Monday weekly market and serves as the main car artery and parking spine into town.

old.name: Es Poal — the cove Dalí painted at fifteen
old.hook: The little shore where the young Dalí set his easel; subject of 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal,' 1920.
old.text: The little shore where the young Dalí set his easel; subject of 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal,' 1920. Es Poal is one of the small calas fringing the bay, a working fishermen's shore of pulled-up boats that the teenage Dalí painted again and again — 'View of Cadaqués from Playa Poal' (1920) frames the white village across the calm water from here, with boats beached in the foreground. Standing on the pebbles, you can line the real bay up against the canvas: the same hump of houses, the same church on top. A short, free, deeply local stop on the waterfront walk. Free; part of the shoreline walk around the bay. · Free. · Anytime. · Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Portlligat
old.text: The sheltered cove 1.2 km north over the hill, a working anchorage of fishing huts that Dalí stitched together into his house from 1930; he lived and painted here until Gala's death in 1982, then moved to Púbol. Now the Casa Salvador Dalí house-museum.

old.name: Coming in August expecting an easy day-trip
old.text: The single GI-614 backs up for kilometres and in-town parking in July-August is brutal; the village's narrow schist lanes can't absorb the load. Instead: Visit in the May-June or Sept-Oct shoulder, or if you must come in August, arrive at dawn and walk in from the outer lots rather than circling.

old.name: Driving out to the Cap de Creus lighthouse in high summer
old.text: The access road beyond the village is closed to private cars on restricted days roughly June-August; you'll be turned back or stuck. Instead: Park free at Corral d'en Morell in town and take the shuttle to the lighthouse, or hike/cycle the coastal track — and check the day's rules with the Parc Natural or Ajuntament first.

old.text: This is one of the windiest stretches of the Catalan coast; gusts over 100 km/h can cancel small-craft movement and make Cap de Creus brutally exposed. Instead: Read the Meteocat / Ports de la Generalitat marine forecast the night before and keep a wind-free fallback (old town, Casa Dalí, a long lunch).
